subject: Post-demo: Locale evaluation playbook & next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sofie Jensen <sofie.jensen@lokalize.io>, Anil Rao <anil@lokalize.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-28T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Locale evaluation playbook & next steps

Hi Sofie / Anil —

Thanks again for the demo call earlier — really helpful to see the Lokalize workflows and the pain points around translations and in-context QA for EU and APAC markets. Quick recap and a concrete plan so we can move into a short model-fit evaluation next week.

Summary of goals (what you said):
- Improve fidelity of translated UI strings and short-form marketing copy (FR, DE).
- Reduce hallucinations and incorrect proper nouns in Japanese and Korean for product descriptions.
- Keep latency under 250ms p50 for synchronous suggestions in the web UI.

Proposed minimal evaluation playbook (we can adjust):
1) Languages in-scope: French (FR), German (DE), Japanese (JP), Korean (KR).
2) For each language, run top-3 candidate models across two prompt patterns: short UI string rewrite and product description expansion.
3) Metrics: exact string overlap / token-level F1 for referenceable items, a small human-judged 5-point accuracy scale for hallucination-prone items, and latency p50/p95.
4) Dataset: start with your 1k sample strings per language (you mentioned a subset). If you can share a drive folder with 500–1,000 short examples per language that represent the failure modes, that will speed the tests.

Initial model recommendations (fast start):
- FR/DE: Llama-2-Chat-13B (q4f16) — good base for short-string fidelity and cost.
- JP/KR: Mistral-Instruct-8B (8-bit) — better tokenization for CJK and lower hallucination observed in our internal runs.
- Fallback: Redwood-1.3-medium (quantized fp16) — predictable latency for synchronous UI.

Attachments I’ve included: locale_prompt_sets_v1.xlsx (seed prompts + expected outputs), benchmark_summary_fr_de_apac.pdf (baseline numbers against open models).

Next steps / owners:
- Lokalize: please drop the 500–1,000 sample strings per language in the Drive folder (link below) by Thu 3/31 — Sofie / Anil
- Redwood: we will run the first pass evals for FR/DE by Mon 4/4 and JP/KR by Wed 4/6 — Marcus
- Redwood Sales/CS: Neha will coordinate a 4-week pilot agreement and confirm data residency / compliance checkpoints — Neha

Notes on compliance and residency: you flagged EU data residency for FR/DE. We can run evaluation on dedicated EU capacity (Private) and provide SOC 2 and DPIA artifacts. Neha — can you pull the pack for Lokalize?

Links:
- Benchmark deck: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/REL-8923
- Lokalize sample folder (please upload samples there): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-lokalize-samples

If this plan looks good I’ll create the HubSpot Mutual Action Plan and we’ll queue the Dedicated EU runs.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the clear plan. Confirming we can deliver the sample sets to the Drive folder by EOD Thu 3/31. We’ll prioritize problematic strings and product description examples for JP and KR.

A few clarifications from our side:
- Data residency: the production content must stay in the EU for FR/DE. Evaluation can run on a staging subset outside the EU for speed, but any pilot that uses real production PII must be on EU Dedicated instances.
- Success criteria: for FR/DE we care most about exact-match for critical UI strings (legal text & button labels) and a human accuracy >= 4/5 for marketing copy. For JP/KR we want a measurable reduction in hallucinations — even a 30% reduction in high-risk hallucinations would be a win.
- Timeline: we’re aiming to sign a 3-month pilot by mid-April if the evaluations look promising.

I’ve uploaded a short sample set of 150 items per language to the Drive folder already to get things started: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-lokalize-samples (see subfolder /starter_150).

On the compliance artifacts: can you share SOC 2 and DPIA docs for review?

— Sofie
